classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Original Host, Datum, Level and fixed complex embedding/type
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: All original number-field, CM host, perfect projective integral datum, level, fixed sigma and ordered type hypotheses remain. The N1c positive-rank guard is retained. No common field or host is constructed.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: The original supplied representing Moduli record
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: The original Xo with quasiprojectivity, smoothness of dimension f*p*q, universal Obj, reduced-scheme representing property and stated infinitesimal field is supplied. The chapter constructs its finite holomorphic FamilyUnif, not Xo itself. Analytic representability is not assumed.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Finite lattices, Dedekind projectivity and tangent derivations
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Finite torsion-free modules over a Dedekind domain are projective; projective modules lift through surjections. Full discrete real lattices are finite free over Z. Standard finite linear algebra, separability idempotents and tangent derivations are used.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF4 uses the actual exponential kernel; HUF5 lifts into the integral target lattice, with no O_E-freeness hypothesis. HUF1 proves the original dual-number dictionary.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Holomorphic local ODE, implicit function and elementary covering theory
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Holomorphic ODE has local solutions holomorphic in parameters. The holomorphic implicit/inverse function theorem, local flows, universal covers, proper local-homeomorphism covering theory, uniform convergence and elementary compact-complex maximum principles are used.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF3 writes the global exponential by division and multiplication. HUF7 proves fullness of the continued lattice by a proper finite covering of degree one, instead of assuming a relative uniformization theorem. HUF8 handles all n through one Chern form.

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Appell-Humbert classification and positivity
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: Hermitian/semicharacter factors classify analytic lines on a complex torus, and positive definite Hermitian form is equivalent to ampleness.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF3 extracts the actual form and KTriv perfection. HUF4 checks the CM adjoint identity. HUF18 uses PUN20 primitive normalization, writes the exact theta factors and verifies the first-linear sign.

references.author: Brian Conrad
references.title: Abelian Varieties: Geometry, Parameter Spaces, and Arithmetic (2005)

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Riemann algebraicity and projective GAGA in the inherited form
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: A positive integral period torus is algebraic; analytic homomorphisms between the resulting projective tori and coherent sheaves/sections on projective complex varieties are algebraic.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: The actual reverse-point fibers already are projective by their printed RelAmple presentation. HUF3 algebraizes the explicit Weil generators. HUF20 uses GAGA only on each projective fiber to supply its algebraic section; no algebraization of an arbitrary analytic base is inferred.

references.author: Brian Conrad
references.title: Abelian Varieties: Geometry, Parameter Spaces, and Arithmetic

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Injective holomorphic maps of equal complex dimension are local biholomorphisms
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: An injective holomorphic map from an open subset of C^d into C^d has nonzero Jacobian determinant and a holomorphic inverse onto its open image.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF11 proves injectivity from PUN23 and verifies both dimensions are the original f*p*q. The d=0 case is explicit.

references.author: Jiri Lebl
references.title: Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4 (31 May 2026)

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Finite connected components of semialgebraic sets
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: A semialgebraic subset of a finite-dimensional real affine space has finitely many connected components.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF13 applies it on a finite affine cover of the complex base change of the supplied Moduli, writing complex equations as real and imaginary polynomial equations. No compactness of Moduli is assumed.

references.author: Michel Coste
references.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry (October 2002)
references.location: Theorem 2.23, p.40; finite cylindrical decomposition Theorem 2.20, p.37

classical_and_foundational_inputs.name: Analytic constant-cohomology direct image and base change
classical_and_foundational_inputs.statement: For a proper holomorphic map to a reduced complex base and a coherent sheaf flat over that base, constant dimension of degree-l fiber cohomology implies locally free degree-l direct image and the fiber base-change isomorphisms.
classical_and_foundational_inputs.application_checked: HUF19 uses l=0, a proper torus submersion and its Hom line, flat locally over a coordinate projection, with h0=1 on every fiber. It then proves global triviality using the rigidification; the theorem alone is not said to trivialize the direct image.
